capabilities.target: Any order, any amount up to the order total, via the payments processor

inputs.source: Support staff refund request via SSO-authenticated chat interface

instructions.note: "Use your judgment on partial refunds" sets no limit on amount, frequency, or justification for partial refunds.

The only stated safeguard is the instruction to "check the order" before issuing a refund; no structural control (approval, cap, scoped credential) backs this instruction, and the prompt explicitly removes confirmation.

controls.name: Human approval gate on refund issuance
Per-staff least-privilege credential for refund and order tools
Per-staff and aggregate refund rate/spend cap

findings.title: Shared service account plus no approval gate lets any authenticated staff member direct irreversible refunds beyond their own authority

attack_path.note: Any SSO-authenticated staff member sends a refund request.
Agent reads order and payment details using the shared service account.
Agent issues an irreversible refund up to the order total using the same shared service account, with no confirmation step.

forecast.watch_signal: A new input source is connected that lets unauthenticated or external parties (customers directly, an external ticketing system, or a partner agent) trigger refund requests without a staff member in the loop.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to check the order then issue the refund using its own judgment on partial amounts, with no requirement to seek approval.
The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool, so the refund capability carries broader privilege than any individual staff member's own access.
cap.issue_refund permits any order and any amount up to the order total, and is irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate on cap.issue_refund that shows the approver the raw destination, order id, and amount (not a model summary), required for every refund above a low fixed threshold.
Replace the shared service account with per-staff delegated credentials scoped to least privilege, so the agent cannot act with more authority than the requesting staff member holds.

findings.title: No attributable record of which staff member authorized a given refund

forecast.watch_signal: Any additional tool is added to the shared service account, or refund volume per staff member per day rises, without a per-staff attribution record being added.

evidence.observation: The processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why.
The agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days.

recommendations.action: Record a tamper-evident, per-refund entry that ties the authenticated staff identity to the order and amount, independent of the ephemeral chat transcript and the service-account-only processor log.
Retain staff request records long enough to support post-incident investigation of disputed or fraudulent refunds, rather than deleting chats after 7 days.

findings.title: No aggregate spend or rate limit on refund issuance beyond the per-order total

forecast.watch_signal: Refund volume or aggregate dollar amount per staff member per day rises without a corresponding cap being added.

evidence.observation: No spend or rate limit beyond the per-order refund amount is described; refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day, so repeated issuance cannot be reversed after the fact.
cap.issue_refund applies to any order and any amount up to the order total, with no aggregate cap mentioned.

recommendations.action: Add a per-staff and aggregate daily/weekly cap on refund amount and count, enforced outside the model.
Add anomaly detection on refund volume and amount per staff identity to flag spikes for review.

stride_coverage.rationale: Staff identity is established via SSO authentication before any request reaches the agent.
No IaC or runtime config was supplied describing integrity protections for the agent's configuration or prompt.
The agent only returns order and refund details to the already-authorized staff member who requested them, and no capability forwards this data elsewhere.
Staff identity is established via SSO authentication before any request reaches the agent.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity controls, such as TLS or request signing, between the agent and the payments processor API.
The payments processor already holds the order and payment details as the system of record; sending the order id and amount is required to execute the refund and discloses nothing new to it.
Artifacts do not describe access controls or write protections on the payments processor's transaction log.
Artifacts do not describe who can query the processor log, which contains amounts and order identifiers.
The log is maintained by the third-party payments processor independent of the agent, and no agent capability can disable or flood it.
Artifacts do not describe access or integrity controls on the staff chat store during its 7-day retention window.
Staff chats may contain customer details or refund justifications and no access control for this store is described.
This chat log does not gate or rate-limit any capability; its unavailability would not enable or block refund issuance.

rating.rationale: The agent holds an S3 sink (irreversible refund spend, up to the full order total) reachable from a trusted but uncontrolled source, with full autonomy (A4, no confirmation step), which raises inherent risk to high. No structural control currently covers the path: there is no approval gate, the credential is a shared service account rather than scoped to the requesting staff member, there is no spend or rate cap, and no record ties a refund to the staff member who requested it. With zero effective controls, residual equals inherent at high for all three findings. The forecast reaches critical because adding any untrusted intake channel (data_scope_expansion, e.g. direct customer requests or an external ticketing integration) would reclassify the source as untrusted against the same unreviewed S3 sink, which the base matrix rates critical. The single highest-leverage fix is a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate on cap.issue_refund, paired with per-staff credential scoping and a per-refund attribution record.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP configuration, IaC, or source code was provided; capability scope, credential handling, and the absence of approval tooling are inferred from prose runtime notes, so confidence on some details is medium.

Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not stated in the artifacts and are recorded as unknown; if undisclosed limits exist, the autonomy classification used here should be revisited.
